findings.title: The active-consumer scanner is fail-open for simple semantic equivalents of forbidden claims
observations: Fixture 'This is not a caveat: x_C=0 proves FLRW isotropy.' matched the forbidden promotion regex but was classified explicit_refutation solely because an unrelated 'not' occurs anywhere in the large context window; unresolved_active_claim_count remained 0.
Fixture 'V2 = W_N2' produced no finding because nilsson_symbol_conflation recognizes only W_N2 on the left-hand side.
Fixture 'W_N2 is identical to V2' produced no finding because natural-language equivalence is not recognized.

The exact forbidden fixture 'x_C=0 proves FLRW isotropy' is automatically allowed when its path is docs/codex_handoff/pr_backlog.yaml because the entire backlog receives registered_candidate disposition without checking card identity or kill-switch locality.
The registered scanner test exercises only one exact positive phrase and does not mutate negation scope, reversed bridge direction, equivalence wording, or backlog locality.
findings.consequence: A claim-language regression can coexist with pass=true, zero unresolved active claims, a passing mutation report, and a PASS terminal route. This defeats the PR-169 all-consumer negative-scan acceptance gate.
required_remediation: Replace window-wide negation detection with match-local, direction-aware refutation handling or fail closed on ambiguity.
Recognize both bridge directions and explicit equivalence paraphrases, or use a typed claim inventory rather than regex-only semantics.
Restrict the backlog exemption to the exact hash-bound PR-169 candidate text/kill-switch record instead of exempting the entire file.
Register and kill the four demonstrated mutations in the production scanner test and mutation report.
findings.kill_switch: Do not accept consumer_gate.pass or mutation_gate=true for PR-169 until all demonstrated variants are detected as unresolved or narrowly proven refutations.

findings.title: The CAS collector can issue CAS_4AXIS_PASS from structurally invalid harness envelopes

nested_payload.omitted: schema, contract identity, obligations/checks, computed exact values, fixtures, commands, tool versions, verified input hashes, source hashes

findings.observed: _collect_version returned CAS_4AXIS_PASS for all four synthetic axes.
findings.consequence: The sealed receipt's aggregate is derived from an unvalidated nested status string. Accidental corruption or a rewritten outer result can be re-sealed as a four-axis pass without demonstrating any CAS obligation, even while the containing result envelope says error.
required_remediation: Validate assignment_sha256 with the canonical assignment hash rule and rehash every required input.
Validate the full outer result envelope: run, assignment, result path, independence mode, claim ID, context version, and status alignment.

Validate the nested schema-v2 CAS result against the contract obligation/check keyset, exact computed values/fixtures, command exits, tool versions, verified input/source hashes, and PASS evidence class before aggregation.
Add malformed-envelope mutations for invalid assignment hash, outer error with nested PASS, missing obligation keys, and drifted required input.
findings.kill_switch: Do not treat collect_pr169_cas_receipts.py as an independent four-axis acceptance gate until malformed envelopes fail before aggregation.

findings.title: Three preserved v1 CAS assignments no longer have their hash-pinned source bytes
observations: All v1 assignment, outer-result, and normalized-result receipt hashes are intact.
The v1 runner hash and contract hash remain intact, but the three engine-specific source paths were overwritten by the v2 repairs.
The collector copies only assignment, outer result, and normalized nested result; it does not archive axis source bytes.
The affected axis files are untracked in the current worktree, so the assignment's baseline commit cannot recover the old bytes.
findings.consequence: The historical v1 CAS_FAIL remains a hash-bound record but cannot be rerun from the preserved receipt. That contradicts the collector's stated purpose of sealing both attempts into durable, replayable receipts and weakens the no-cross-version-reuse audit trail.
required_remediation: Restore the exact v1 Wolfram, SymPy, and Sage source bytes under immutable versioned paths, or archive their bytes in the v1 receipt tree with hashes.

Point the v1 durable assignments and replay commands at those immutable versioned sources without rewriting the original receipt evidence; use a separate provenance index if receipt immutability forbids path edits.
Add a collection check that rehashes every versioned assignment required input and reports historical-source unavailability explicitly.
findings.kill_switch: Do not describe the v1 attempt as replayable until all hash-pinned input bytes are available; describe it only as preserved historical failure evidence meanwhile.
